extracted.intended_audience: guideline developers, implementers, health services researchers, and policymakers interested in clinical guideline implementation
extracted.subtask_description: A systematic meta-review synthesizing evidence from systematic reviews about factors that positively or negatively influence implementation (use/adherence/compliance) of clinical guidelines for health care professionals. It also assesses methodological quality of included reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criteria for meta-review (systematic review definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only systematic reviews or meta-reviews were eligible. A review was considered systematic if at least two of the following three criteria were satisfied: (a) search terms are presented; (b) Pubmed/Medline, at least, has been searched; (c) the methodological quality of the included studies has been assessed by the reviewer(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also required that the reviews' guidelines be aimed at medical staff, nurses or other health care professionals and that the reviews discuss factors that influence guideline implementation either positively or negatively. No limits on language or search period were applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion criteria for meta-review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews or meta-reviews exclusively focused on consensus procedures or consensus-based guidelines were excluded. Reviews that did not differentiate conclusions between clinical guidelines and other professional interventions (e.g., continuing education or comprehensive quality programs) were excluded. Reviews whose findings were not only based on research publications but also on descriptive, narrative or theoretical articles were excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exclusions reflect the authors' emphasis on evidence-based guideline literature and on isolating factors specific to guideline implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy and study selection procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct comprehensive database searches (PubMed, CINAHL, Cochrane library, Embase, NIVEL catalogues, GIN) with an explicit search strategy; import references into reference manager; remove duplicates; perform a two-step inclusion process: (1) screening on the basis of references and abstracts, (2) screening based on full-text papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen titles/abstracts and full texts independently by at least two reviewers; perform reference tracking/manual searches; resolve disagreements by discussion; record flow (e.g., number found, screened, full texts assessed, included). Limit search results to items with abstracts and exclude letters/comments/editorials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological quality assessment of reviews (Quality Assessment Checklist for Reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess methodological quality of included reviews using the Quality Assessment Checklist for Reviews (Oxman & Guyatt). The checklist items align with QUORUM and documented psychometric properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist yields overall scores interpreted as: 'extensive flaws' (score 1 or 2), 'major flaws' (score 3 or 4), 'minor flaws' (score 5 or 6), 'minimal flaws' (score 7). Important checklist elements include: description of search strategy, comprehensiveness of search, clear inclusion criteria, use of more than one reviewer to prevent selection bias, and systematic assessment of methodological quality of included studies. When reviewers' scores differ, average scores or discussion should be used; large differences (>1 point) require consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of factors influencing implementation (five categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors that influence implementation are to be classified in the following categories: characteristics of the guidelines; characteristics of the implementation strategies; characteristics of professionals; characteristics of patients; characteristics of the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This categorization facilitates synthesis and comparison across reviews and was chosen for compatibility with prior classifications (e.g., Cabana et al., Simpson et al.). Data extraction should follow this structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline characteristic: complexity (understandability, trialability, resource needs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines that are easy to understand, can easily be tried out, and do not require specific resources have a greater chance of being used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complexity is the most frequently described guideline characteristic influencing implementation. For multi-disciplinary guidelines aimed at diverse target groups, developers should aim for clarity and usability across educational levels; testing guidelines in practice before large-scale implementation is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline characteristic: evidence base and development involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines with a clear scientific base (evidence-based) appear to have higher adherence. Involving the target group and relevant experts in guideline development can enhance successful implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings about end-user development increasing use are not unanimous across reviews; more research is needed. AGREE and WHO recommendations to include broad composition of development groups are cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation strategy characteristic: multi-faceted vs single strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation strategies may be single (e.g., reminders, a single educational intervention) or multi-faceted (combinations of components such as educational materials, meetings, audit and feedback, reminders, system redesign, additional resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most reviews indicate that effective strategies often have multiple components and that single strategies are less effective; however, high-quality evidence is sparse and findings are sometimes contradictory (e.g., Grimshaw et al. found modest effects and no clear relation between number of components and effectiveness). Context, intensity, and integration into care processes matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation strategy characteristic: proximity to end user and active participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies that require active professional participation and that are closely related to clinical decision-making are more likely to succeed. Interventions integrated into the process of care and 'closer to the end user' tend to be more effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include web-based/written/face-to-face practical recommendations, educational meetings, and combining these with tools integrated into workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation strategy characteristic: intensity, comprehensiveness, and system redesign
rubrics_metrics.description: Intensive, comprehensive strategies that may involve system redesign or additional resources (e.g., extra consultation time, case management) can be more successful—particularly in some fields such as mental health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some lower-quality reviews report multi-faceted, intensive interventions as most successful, but methodological differences and topic heterogeneity may explain contradictions across reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional characteristic: awareness, familiarity, and agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A lack of awareness of guidelines, limited familiarity with content, and lack of agreement with guideline recommendations are main barriers to adoption among professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted implementation interventions that create awareness and actively involve professionals are recommended; mere dissemination is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional characteristic: demographic/experience factors and involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Age and experience may influence uptake (younger or less experienced professionals may be more inclined to use guidelines). Involvement of the target professionals in development may enhance implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence for some of these associations is limited and sometimes contradictory; interpret cautiously due to methodological limitations in underlying reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient characteristic: co-morbidity and resistance/perceived need
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient factors that influence guideline adherence include co-morbidity (which reduces adherence because guidelines may be seen as insufficiently tailored) and patient resistance or perceived lack of need for recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline developers should consider multimorbidity and provide guidance tailored to patients with multiple conditions; attention to patients' attitudes and expectations is important for implementers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental characteristic: resources and social support
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental factors such as insufficient staff, limited time, high work pressure, and lack of support from peers or superiors negatively influence guideline implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation plans must consider organizational support, staffing, protected time, and leadership endorsement to improve uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence synthesis practice: avoid pooling when heterogeneity large
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of large variety in factors described and methods used across reviews, quantitative pooling was not performed; many reviews do not provide effect sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusions should be based on the synthesized results and the reviews' own conclusions; where possible, rigorous reviews should account for effect sizes and heterogeneous contexts. Future research should use sound designs that allow comparison of combinations of strategies vs single strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data extraction and checking procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Data extraction should be performed by one reviewer and subsequently checked by another reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent assessment and checking reduce errors; disagreements in decisions about inclusion or quality scoring should be resolved by discussion between reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation caveat: methodological quality affects conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Many included reviews scored low or middle ranges on the Quality Assessment Checklist for Reviews, indicating a high likelihood of extensive or major flaws, which should temper confidence in their findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The meta-reviewers decided to include lower-quality reviews to present a complete picture but advise caution and recommend more methodologically rigorous future research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for implementers and guideline researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementers should plan targeted, multi-component interventions that actively engage end users and integrate into clinical workflows; researchers should conduct rigorous empirical research comparing combinations of implementation strategies versus single strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although multiple strategies appear to be more effective overall, evidence is thin and sometimes contradictory; better-designed studies with clear effect size reporting and context description are needed.
